title: Sculpture
examples: Can you show me an example of casting?
Is carving always done with stone?

explain.say: Today we are learning about sculpture. Sculpture is art created in three dimensions. It takes up space all around you.
First we look at carving. Carving means removing material from a solid block. Think about cutting away stone or wood.
Next is modelling. Modelling involves shaping soft material like clay. You build up the form layer by layer.
Casting is when you make a copy of an original sculpture. You use a mold to pour liquid material into it.

draw.text: Casting: Making a copy in a mold

explain.say: A famous example of carving is the bust of David. This sculpture was carved from a single block of marble.
Another famous example is the Venus de Milo. This statue was originally modelled and then cast in marble.

faq.q: What is the main difference between carving and casting?
faq.a: Carving means taking material away from a solid block, while casting means making a copy using a mold.
asks: Does casting require an original piece?
How is casting different from carving?

faq.q: Can I carve wood or only stone?
faq.a: No, you can carve many materials, including wood, soap, and even some types of plastic.
asks: What materials are good for carving?

faq.q: Is modelling the same as sculpting?
faq.a: Modelling is a way to sculpt, but it specifically refers to shaping soft materials like clay.
asks: Is modelling a type of sculpture?
What is the difference between modelling and casting?

faq.q: Do all famous sculptures use these three methods?
faq.a: No, some sculptures might combine techniques, like modelling first and then casting the final piece.
asks: Are there other ways to make statues?

faq.q: What is a mold used for in sculpture?
faq.a: A mold creates a negative space, which allows you to pour a new material to make a copy.
asks: What is the purpose of a mold?

facts: Carving involves subtracting material from a solid block.
Modelling uses pliable materials like clay to build up a form.
Casting requires creating a mold to capture a shape.
Bronze is a common material used in casting.

quiz.say: A sculptor removes chips from a block of limestone to create a statue. Which technique did they use?
quiz.why: Carving is the process of removing material from a solid piece.

wrong.1: Modelling is about adding material to build up the shape.
wrong.2: Casting requires making a copy using a mold.
wrong.3: Building is too general; carving is the specific term for removal.

quiz.say: To make a replica of a statue using liquid metal, the artist must first create a:
quiz.why: A mold is necessary to hold the liquid material while it hardens around the shape.

wrong.0: A block is the starting material, not what holds the liquid.
wrong.1: Clay is a material used for modelling, not for making the container.
wrong.2: Tools are used to create the mold, but they are not the mold itself.

quiz.say: If an artist starts with soft clay and builds up a figure, they are most likely:
quiz.why: Modelling specifically describes the action of shaping soft, pliable materials.

wrong.1: Carving means cutting away material, not adding it.
wrong.2: Casting requires a mold and a liquid material to fill it.
wrong.3: Sculpting is the general term; modelling is the specific action with clay.
